correctness.rationale: The three named reflexive relations and two distinct singleton colours are essential. Row/column preservation makes an automorphism a pair of bijections; the sum condition forces both to be translates of one additive bijection, which is F₂-linear. The two fixed marks reduce this to the pointwise stabilizer of H. Equal κ profiles give a map fixing H and taking x,y to x′,y′ that is well defined on H+span(x,y): the only nonempty subset sums of the two generators are x,y,x+y, and the profiles agree on all their values in H. Extend this isomorphism to the whole space. Counting the cases of zero, one, and two independent images modulo H gives the asserted fibre sizes and census. A round-one cell at the intersection of two differently directed named marker lines is singleton. The listed witnesses cover H in each projection for both r=1 and r=2, allowing round two to read κ; orbit invariance forbids further splitting. For the exact depth, r=2 has distinct H² cells (v,u+v) and (u+v,u) on none of the marker lines. With r=1 and normalized B=(w,0), independent outside quotient images give the collision between (s,w) and (s,t). At quotient dimension one in the r=1 case every profile outside H² has exactly one known H-value. The only such profile not directly named by a marker line is the column value w; it is then uniquely recognized by an empty marker-line signature. At d=1 all cells are witnesses. Independent enumeration of all 336 normalized marker configurations in dimensions 1–4 (69,564 cell instances) checked exact partitions, class sizes and first recovery rounds.
